stories.title: Nuveen Green Capital Closes $173M C-PACE Loan on Miami-Area Condos Project
stories.excerpt: The continued strength of Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy (C-PACE) debt as a construction financing tool has made a big splash in South Florida. Miami developer Shoma Group has landed a $172.5 million C-PACE loan from Nuveen Green Capital to develop its Shoma Bay mixed-use condominium waterfront project in North Bay Village, Fla., Commercial Observer can first report. This transaction provides further evidence of the power of C-PACE to provide accretive financing for large-scale assets such as Shoma Bay,” Ryan Doyle, senior director of originations, at Nuveen Green Capital, said in a statement. “The project is particularly impactful, as Nuveen Green Capital served as the sole capital provider for this development, which ranks among the five largest C-PACE-financed projects in the state of Florida.” Doyle originated the loan with a Nuveen Green Capital team that also featured Christopher Lawton, head of originations, along with Brendan Moore, director, and Tyler Amano, associate director. One source familiar with the transaction said it’s notable because there’s no other debt provider in the capital stack — just the C-PACE loan, condo sales deposits and equity. Located at 1850 John F. Kennedy Causeway 10 miles northeast of Downtown Miami, the 24-story Shoma Bay development will comprise 333 condo units and retail space anchored by a 36,000-square-foot Publix supermarket. Community amenities will include a rooftop pool deck, a wellness spa, a two-story fitness center, a padel court and coworking spaces. Newmark negotiated the debt with a team consisting of Anthony Orso, Clifford Welden, Daniel Matz and Henry Stimler. “Shoma Bay is an exceptional project that reflects the continued evolution of North Bay Village into one of South Florida’s most dynamic waterfront communities,” Orso said in a statement. Shoma Group did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Nuveen Green Capital closes $172.5M C-PACE construction loan for Shoma Group's Miami condo project
Shoma Bay mixed-use waterfront development in North Bay Village, among top 5 C-PACE deals in Florida
C-PACE proves viable as sole capital source for large-scale residential mixed-use projects in South Florida
stories.summary: Nuveen Green Capital provided a $172.5 million C-PACE (Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy) construction loan to Miami developer Shoma Group for Shoma Bay, a mixed-use waterfront condominium project in North Bay Village. This marks one of the five largest C-PACE-financed projects in Florida, with Nuveen serving as the sole capital provider. C-PACE continues to demonstrate strength as a construction financing tool for large-scale residential assets in South Florida.
stories.impact: C-PACE availability as a construction financing tool directly reduces reliance on traditional construction debt in South Florida, expanding feasibility for large mixed-use residential developments. This capital alternative may enable developers to pursue projects at lower all-in costs or with more favorable terms, pressuring traditional lenders' pricing and increasing competitive supply of rental units in the Miami/South Florida market.

stories.title: Related Ross Buys Land for Major Mixed-Use Dev in Florida
stories.excerpt: Billionaire Stephen Ross has closed on a land acquisition to build a major, open-air mixed-use development in Wellington, a village in Palm Beach County, Fla., renowned for its equestrian scene. Related Ross, the developer’s namesake firm, paid $28.3 million for a 32-acre site at 10400 Stribling Way, just east of State Road 7, property records show. The planned development, called Village Landing, is set to include a 180-room hotel and over 300,000 square feet of retail, office and restaurant space, all connected by six plazas. “Our goal is to create a village center that complements what is already special about Wellington while adding the everyday amenities, restaurants, experiences and connections that are designed to serve the western communities of Palm Beach County,” Kevin Ryan, executive vice president of Related Ross, said in a statement. Starwood Property Trust supplied a $29.1 million loan. Construction is expected to commence in the fall. The western portion of the site, spanning about 44 acres, will be turned into a private grade school, operated by ElevateED. The land sale is expected to close in October, per a representative for Related Ross. The combined 71-acre parcel is part of the Acme Improvement District, which was controlled by the Village of Wellington. In 1953, the Florida Legislature created the special district to manage water drainage and infrastructure development. Village Landing marks Related Ross’ first ground-up development outside of West Palm Beach since launching in 2024 and becoming the city’s biggest office owner. Ross’s goal is to turn West Palm Beach into a leading business hub and attract high-profile tech and finance companies. The West Palm Beach-based firm is building two more office buildings after securing a $772 million construction loan package last year. Two luxury condo developments are under construction. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Related Ross acquires 32-acre site in Wellington, Palm Beach County for $28.3 million
Village Landing mixed-use: 180-room hotel, 300K+ SF retail/office/restaurant across six plazas; construction Q4 2024
Starwood Property Trust finances deal with $29.1M construction loan; targets western Palm Beach County communities
stories.summary: Related Ross closed a $28.3 million land acquisition for a 32-acre site in Wellington, Palm Beach County, Florida, to develop Village Landing, a major mixed-use project. The planned development includes a 180-room hotel, over 300,000 square feet of retail, office, and restaurant space, and six plazas designed to serve western Palm Beach County communities. Starwood Property Trust provided a $29.1 million construction loan, with groundbreaking expected in fall 2024.
stories.impact: Related's $28.3M land deal in the equestrian-focused Wellington submarket signals confidence in western Palm Beach County demand for mixed-use retail/hospitality anchors, implying population density and affluent household migration supporting future multifamily development in adjacent areas. Development of convenience/lifestyle amenities typically precedes or accompanies multifamily infill in secondary submarkets.

stories.title: Tucson Walmart SuperCenter Opens September 2
stories.excerpt: Out with the old, in with the new. Walmart will celebrate the conversion of its East Wetmore Road store into a full-service Supercenter on Wednesday, Sept. 2,. The store will be about 180,000 square feet. The store at 455 E. Wetmore Road was Tucson’s last remaining Walmart general merchandise location. Following the conversion, customers can now purchase fresh groceries, fill prescriptions and complete a full weekly shopping trip at the property. The upgraded Supercenter includes an expanded fresh grocery department with produce, meat, dairy and frozen foods, along with a new deli and bakery. Walmart also updated the pharmacy with an additional private consultation room and expanded merchandise selections in automotive, fashion, consumables and health and wellness. The post Tucson Walmart SuperCenter Opens September 2 appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Walmart converts Tucson East Wetmore Road store to 180K-SF SuperCenter on September 2
Upgrade adds fresh grocery, deli, bakery, pharmacy, expanded retail; last Walmart general merchandise location in Tucson
Retail anchor activation in Tucson signals neighborhood investment and potential demand driver for nearby residential
stories.summary: Walmart is converting its East Wetmore Road location in Tucson into a full-service 180,000-square-foot SuperCenter on September 2, adding fresh groceries, deli, bakery, and pharmacy services. This was Tucson's last remaining Walmart general merchandise location, making this conversion a significant retail upgrade for the area.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily development strategy. Retail anchors can signal neighborhood stability and foot traffic in secondary markets, but a single conversion does not materially shift demand or supply signals for apartment development in Tucson.

stories.title: Investor General Atlantic to Anchor Related’s 625 Madison Avenue in 150K-SF Deal
stories.excerpt: Related Companies just nabbed an anchor tenant for its under-construction office tower at 625 Madison Avenue in Manhattan’s Plaza District, the developer announced Tuesday. General Atlantic, a global investment firm, has inked a long-term lease to occupy more than 150,000 square feet across five floors at the planned 53-story office tower, which is slated to open in 2029. The firm will use the space for its more than 330 New York-based employees, who represent about one-third of the company’s global workforce. “General Atlantic has always taken a long-term view, and our new headquarters is an investment in the firm’s future,” Bill Ford, chairman and CEO of General Atlantic, said in a statement. “It will be a place that brings our people and global community together, strengthens the connections that are central to who we are, and gives us room to grow for many decades to come.” The exact length of the lease and the asking rent were not disclosed. The average asking rent for Class A office space in the Plaza District was $97.23 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to Colliers data. Related did not disclose the names of the brokers who worked on this deal. “When we began designing 625 Madison, General Atlantic was exactly the kind of prestigious and ambitious firm we had in mind as an anchor tenant because of the value they place on investment and operational excellence, collaboration and long-term relationships,” Jeff Blau, CEO of Related, said in a statement. “This will be a building of industry leaders, and we are thrilled to have General Atlantic on board and look forward to delivering an exceptional new headquarters for their team.” In tandem with General Atlantic’s lease, private equity firm Veritas Capital has also seemed to secure new office space at 625 Madison Avenue. In August, Veritas signed a lease for 92,743 square feet at the office development, according to Colliers’ August Manhattan office snapshot report. Spokespeople for Veritas
bullets: General Atlantic leases 150K+ SF across five floors at Related's 625 Madison Avenue, Manhattan Plaza District
Long-term lease for investment firm's 330+ NY employees (one-third of global workforce); tower opens 2029
Class A Plaza District average asking rent: $97.23/SF; major corporate anchor pre-lease signals strong office demand recovery
stories.summary: Related Companies secured General Atlantic, a global investment firm, as an anchor tenant for its under-construction 53-story office tower at 625 Madison Avenue in Manhattan's Plaza District. General Atlantic will occupy over 150,000 square feet across five floors on a long-term lease for its 330+ New York-based employees, representing approximately one-third of the firm's global workforce. The tower is slated to open in 2029.
stories.impact: General Atlantic's long-term, pre-lease commitment to 625 Madison signals sustained demand for Class A office space and executive presence in Manhattan, supporting office-to-residential conversion potential and cross-asset demand for luxury multifamily near the Plaza District. Employer stability and headcount expansion in Manhattan support rental demand in nearby residential markets.

stories.title: Work Wraps Up on 74-Story Austin Mixed-Use Tower
stories.excerpt: Lincoln Property Co. and Kairoi Residential wrapped up construction on Waterline, the Lone Star State’s tallest tower, rising 74 stories in downtown Austin, Texas. The mixed-use property features 352 multifamily units across 33 levels, 703,000 square feet of office space spanning 24 floors and 252 hotel keys taking up 13 stories. Multihousing New reports Waterline is subject to a $742.5 million self-financed construction loan originated in June 2022, one year before work began. The development team included general contractor DPR Construction and designer KPF. HKS served as the architect of record. The team delivered the project two months ahead of schedule. Bosque Residences represents Waterline’s multifamily portion, encompassing one- to three-bedroom units, including penthouse layouts, that range between 701 and 2,803 square feet. Select apartments include waterfall islands, free-standing tubs, as well as wet and dry bars, among other features. Community amenities include a coworking lounge, conference rooms, a podcast space, a poker venue, a golf simulator, in addition to several swimming pools. The post Work Wraps Up on 74-Story Austin Mixed-Use Tower appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Lincoln Property/Kairoi complete 74-story Waterline tower in downtown Austin; Texas's tallest building
352 multifamily units, 703K SF office, 252 hotel keys; $742.5M self-financed construction loan from June 2022
Bosque Residences apartments (701–2,803 SF) delivered two months ahead of schedule; mixed-use anchors coworking, pools, dining
stories.summary: Lincoln Property Company and Kairoi Residential completed Waterline, a 74-story mixed-use tower in downtown Austin and Texas's tallest building. The project includes 352 multifamily units across 33 levels, 703,000 square feet of office space, and 252 hotel keys. Financed by a $742.5 million self-financed construction loan from June 2022, Waterline was delivered two months ahead of schedule and features luxury unit sizes (701–2,803 SF) and premium amenities.
stories.impact: Waterline's successful completion and on-time delivery of 352 units in downtown Austin demonstrates sustained multifamily development appetite and execution capability in a high-growth, office-anchor market. The mixed-use, self-financed structure with office and hotel reduces financing risk; early delivery signals strong absorption and rental demand in downtown Austin, supporting pipeline confidence for competing and adjacent multifamily projects.

stories.title: Trump Pushes Federal Film Tax Incentive as Hollywood Crisis Deepens
stories.excerpt: President Donald Trump is calling on Congress to create a federal tax incentive for film and television production in what could be a major boost to Hollywood and the other drowning studio and soundstage markets in the U.S. Trump said he is arranging meetings with leaders of both parties to start forming legislation. The president did not specify the size or structure, but a proposal backed by industry heads calls for a 20 percent credit on U.S. production labor costs. While 39 states offer production incentives, the U.S. has no nationwide program comparable to incentives available in several competing countries. “Congress should approve, immediately, a Federal Production Incentive to create Entertainment Jobs in America,” Trump wrote, arguing that film production has migrated to Canada and other countries. The push comes amid an increasingly dire environment for production space and for the entertainment industry that has defined Los Angeles and driven its economy. L.A. County shooting days fell 42 percent between their 2022 peak and 2024, while Southern California production was estimated last year to be 50 to 70 percent below its peak. At the time, roughly half of L.A.’s film and television stages were reportedly empty. Conditions quickly translated into significant distress for studio landlords. Hackman Capital Partners defaulted on $1.1 billion in financing tied to the 1.2 million-square-foot Radford Studio Center, which Goldman Sachs subsequently took control of. Hackman and Affinius Capital had paid $1.85 billion for the property in 2021 and envisioned a $1 billion expansion. Prominent studio complex Television City, where Hackman planned a roughly $1 billion redevelopment, has also fallen into distress, with lenders alleging the landlord owes more than $357 million on the 25-acre property. Hudson Pacific Properties is also grappling with the production downturn and faces a $1.1 billion Hollywood studio loan maturity while its star tenant Netflix pursues Hack
bullets: Trump pushes federal film tax incentive for U.S. production as Hollywood crisis deepens
L.A. County shooting days fell 42% between 2022 peak and 2024; 39 states offer production incentives, U.S. lacks federal program
Proposed 20% credit on U.S. production labor costs would compete with Canada and other countries offering subsidies
stories.summary: President Trump is calling on Congress to create a federal tax incentive for film and television production to address declining Hollywood production activity. L.A. County shooting days dropped 42 percent between 2022 and 2024, and film production has migrated to Canada and other countries offering incentives. A proposed 20 percent credit on U.S. production labor costs is being discussed, though no specific structure or size has been announced.
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily development. A federal film incentive could stabilize Los Angeles entertainment employment and reverse population/talent out-migration, indirectly supporting longer-term rental demand in LA submarkets. However, the near-term outlook for Hollywood employment remains uncertain, and any benefit to multifamily demand would lag incentive implementation by years.

stories.title: Walton Street Capital Refis Tampa-Area Apartments With $44M Loan
stories.excerpt: A joint venture between Mast Capital and Rockpoint has sealed a $44 million loan to refinance a newly completed garden-style apartment community in a suburb north of Tampa, Fla., Commercial Observer has learned. Walton Street Capital supplied the three-year, floating-rate loan on the sponsorship’s248-unit the Harlow property in Wesley Chapel, Fla. The refi retired a past construction loan obtained for the property while providing the borrower flexibility to pursue a sale or permanent financing in the next few years, according to Berkadia, which arranged the transaction. Berkadia negotiated the debt with a team consisting of Mitch Sinberg, Scott Wadler, Matthew Robbins, Brad Williamson and Bryan Brown. “The Harlow presented a compelling financing opportunity given the strength of the sponsorship, quality of the newly built asset and its strong operating performance,” Wadler, managing director at Berkadia, said in a statement. Robbins added the Wesley Chapel submarket benefits from “strong population growth” along with the community’s “significant investment” in retail, health care and infrastructure projects. The property is half a mile north of the $250 million BayCare Hospital Wesley Chapel that opened in 2023. Located at 5301 Bruce B Downs Boulevard 23 miles north of Downtown Tampa, the 2024-built Harlow was 98 percent occupied at the time of the loan with a mix of one-, two- and three-bedroom units. Community amenities include a pool, a sundeck, a fitness center, a walking trail, electronic vehicle charging stations and coworking spaces. “The Harlow’s strong leasing performance reflects the quality of the community and the continued demand we see across the Wesley Chapel market,” Camilo Miguel Jr., founder and CEO of Mast Capital, said in a statement. “This refinancing positions the asset well for its next phase and underscores our conviction in the long-term fundamentals of the Tampa region.” Walton Street Capital did not immediately return a request for c
bullets: Walton Street Capital refinances 248-unit Harlow garden-style apartments in Wesley Chapel, Tampa-area with $44M floating-rate loan
Three-year refi on newly completed Mast Capital/Rockpoint JV property; retires construction loan, enables future sale/permanent refinancing
Wesley Chapel submarket benefits from strong population growth; new asset demonstrates strong operating performance post-delivery
stories.summary: A joint venture between Mast Capital and Rockpoint refinanced the newly completed 248-unit Harlow apartment community in Wesley Chapel, a Tampa-area suburb, with a $44 million three-year floating-rate loan from Walton Street Capital. The refi retired construction debt and provides flexibility for a potential sale or permanent financing within three years. Berkadia arranged the transaction.
stories.impact: Walton Street's willingness to refinance garden-style product in Wesley Chapel at completion signals confidence in Tampa-area suburban demand and operating performance. The three-year floating-rate structure indicates lenders expect rate stability and/or strong market fundamentals; successful placement supports continued multifamily development feasibility in Tampa's outer suburbs, particularly in high-growth corridors like Wesley Chapel.

stories.title: 17-Story Denver Office Tower Trades for $3.6M
stories.excerpt: A number of Denver office towers continue to suffer profitability issues. The 17-story tower, once known as Columbine Place, has been bought for $3.63 million. The Denver Business Journal reports building values in downtown Denver have dropped significantly since then. Adio Palace is the buyer. The building will also be called Adio Palace. The 149,222-square-foot skyscraper previously served as collateral for a $15.5 million loan in 2015. The new owner plans to continue to use the property as is and attract more tenants to the building. The building is 69% vacant. A Denver District Court judge placed the tower into receivership in 2023. The University of Hawaii Foundation held a ground lease on the land while an investor group called Columbine West 2 owned the building. Court documents in 2023 showed Columbine West 2 owed $17.7 million on the building. A foreclosure began after Columbine West 2 had failed to make principal and interest payments since October 2022. The post 17-Story Denver Office Tower Trades for $3.6M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: 17-story Columbine Place office tower in downtown Denver trades for $3.63 million; 69% vacant
Prior $15.5M loan (2015) written down sharply; foreclosure after owner defaulted since October 2022; court receivership in 2023
New owner Adio Palace plans to continue office use and attract tenants; downtown Denver values dropped significantly
stories.summary: A 17-story Denver office tower, formerly known as Columbine Place, sold for $3.63 million after foreclosure and court receivership. The 149,222-square-foot building is currently 69 percent vacant and was previously collateral for a $15.5 million loan in 2015. Court documents showed the owner owed $17.7 million before default began in October 2022. The new owner, Adio Palace, plans to continue operating it as office space.
stories.impact: Downtown Denver's office distress (69% vacancy, sharp valuation decline) signals weak office demand and persistent capitalization headwinds in the metro. Multifamily developers should view downtown Denver office collapse as a risk factor for near-term office-to-residential conversion economics and as evidence of weak white-collar employment/migration in the core, though suburban Denver submarkets may offer stronger demand fundamentals.

stories.title: Broadstone Inks Hobby Lobby, Academy Sports as Manor Tenants
stories.excerpt: Broadstone Net Lease (BNL) secured land in Manor and started construction on build-to-suit developments for Hobby Lobby and Academy Sports, both of which were directly sourced, off-market transactions, and are expected to deliver in the second quarter of 2027. Hobby Lobby and Academy will be 55,000 square feet, and each is on a 15-year lease. Hobby Lobby’s lease has annual rent escalations of 0.5%, and Academy’s lease has 0.4% annual rent escalations. Broadstone is targeting the second quarter of 2027 to deliver the projects. BNL is an industrial-focused, diversified net lease REIT that invests primarily in single-tenant commercial real estate properties net leased on a long-term basis. BNL’s diversified portfolio consisted of 766 individual net-leased commercial properties with 759 properties located in 44 U.S. states and seven properties located in four Canadian provinces across the industrial, retail, and other property types. Academy plans to open 20 to 25 new stores in fiscal year 2026. The post Broadstone Inks Hobby Lobby, Academy Sports as Manor Tenants appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Broadstone Net Lease (BNL) secures land in Manor, Texas; build-to-suit for Hobby Lobby (55K SF) and Academy Sports (55K SF)
Both 15-year leases with low annual escalations (0.5% and 0.4%); delivery Q2 2027; off-market, direct-sourced transactions
Academy Sports plans 20–25 new store openings in fiscal 2026; signals retail expansion driving industrial demand in Texas
stories.summary: Broadstone Net Lease secured land in Manor, Texas, and commenced construction on two build-to-suit projects: a 55,000-square-foot Hobby Lobby and a 55,000-square-foot Academy Sports. Both tenants signed 15-year leases with minimal annual rent escalations (0.5% and 0.4% respectively) and are expected to deliver in Q2 2027. Academy Sports has announced plans for 20–25 new store openings in fiscal 2026.
stories.impact: Academy Sports expansion (20–25 new stores in FY2026) and Hobby Lobby new-market entry signal retail growth and consumer spending activity in Texas, particularly in secondary/tertiary markets like Manor. This retail/logistics activity typically precedes or co-occurs with population migration and multifamily demand; developers should monitor Academy Sports store rollout corridors for future multifamily opportunity sites.

stories.title: Logistics Property Lands Tenant for 217K-SF Houston-Area Warehouse
stories.excerpt: Logistics Property Company leased 217,758 square feet of build-to-suit warehouse space at CityPark Logistics Center, Building 7 in Missouri City, Texas, with Standex GRID / Amran Instrument Transformers (Standex GRID / Amran). Standex GRID / Amran will use the space as both a warehouse and manufacturing facility. CityPark Logistics Center is a 98-acre industrial park that includes five fully leased buildings totaling more than one million square feet. Construction on the new facility is underway, with an anticipated completion in Q2 2027. This new building will be Standex GRID / Amran’s largest North American location. CityPark Logistics Center was selected for its Southwest Houston location and its ability to accommodate a layout that meets Standex GRID/Amran’s office, production, and manufacturing needs. Cushman & Wakefield’s Beau Kaleel and Brooke Swerdlow assisted in the transaction. Standex GRID / Amran was represented by Steve King and Wesley King of CBRE. The general contractor is Burton Construction, with Powers Brown as the architect and Pape Dawson as the civil engineer.  The post Logistics Property Lands Tenant for 217K-SF Houston-Area Warehouse appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Logistics Property Company leases 217,758 SF build-to-suit warehouse to Standex GRID/Amran in Missouri City, Houston-area
Facility serves as warehouse and manufacturing; Standex GRID/Amran's largest North American location; completion Q2 2027
CityPark Logistics Center: 98-acre industrial park, 5 fully leased buildings, 1M+ SF; Southwest Houston location selected for logistics corridor strength
stories.summary: Logistics Property Company leased 217,758 square feet of build-to-suit warehouse and manufacturing space at CityPark Logistics Center, Building 7 in Missouri City, Texas, to Standex GRID/Amran. This will be Standex GRID/Amran's largest North American facility. CityPark Logistics Center is a fully leased 98-acre industrial park with over one million square feet across five buildings. Construction is underway with expected completion in Q2 2027.
stories.impact: Southwest Houston industrial park strength (CityPark fully leased, new major tenant commitment) indicates sustained logistics and manufacturing employment growth, supporting working-class and middle-income multifamily demand in surrounding corridors. High industrial absorption in Missouri City/Southwest Houston submarkets suggests population inflow and wage-earning households, creating tailwinds for workforce and market-rate multifamily development in adjacent residential areas.
